3.1.1.locator: Docs 'Configure HTTP clients' (connections to Baseten inference endpoints): 'Each new HTTP client opens a fresh TCP connection, performs a full TLS handshake...' — i.e. the inference API is served over TLS/HTTPS. Terms/DPA security-measures language: 'commercially available industry standard encryption technologies for personal data that is transmitted over public networks (i.e., the Internet) or when transmitted wirelessly or at rest or stored on portable or removable media'
3.1.1.notes: Real standard: TLS/HTTPS — the negotiated TLS VERSION (1.2 vs 1.3) is not published anywhere retrieved this session, so per the form rule the dropdown must be 'Others - pls indicate below' with 'TLS (version not publicly documented; vendor to confirm minimum enforced version)' in the free-text row. Do NOT write 'TLS 1.2'/'TLS 1.3' without vendor confirmation. Snippet-sourced; direct fetch blocked, and an empirical TLS handshake against Baseten endpoints was impossible (gateway blocks CONNECT).

3.1.2.notes: Baseten's own pages state that data at rest IS encrypted — Terms/DPA security-measures language commits to 'commercially available industry standard encryption technologies' for personal data 'at rest or stored on portable or removable media' (baseten.co/terms-and-conditions/), the enterprise page says model weights and source code are protected 'using advanced encryption' (baseten.co/enterprise/), and docs describe encrypted secrets storage (docs.baseten.co/organization/secrets) — but NO page retrieved this session names the algorithm (AES-128/192/256 etc.), so the dropdown cannot be answered beyond 'Not known'. A targeted domain-restricted search for 'AES-256' across baseten.co, docs.baseten.co and trust.baseten.co returned no algorithm claim. The specific standard is likely in the SOC 2 report on file in Vanta or the gated SafeBase trust center — check there before emailing the vendor. Mitigating context: Baseten's default posture is zero data retention — model inputs/outputs are not stored by default (docs.baseten.co/observability/security).

3.1.3.notes: Backup encryption is not documented anywhere on Baseten's public pages retrieved this session ('Not known' is the playbook-expected answer for most vendors here). The trust center summary lists 'backups' among covered technical details (authentication mechanisms, backups, firewall configurations, data encryption, and cypher suites) but the detail is gated behind the SafeBase access request. Note the mitigating control: Baseten does not store model inputs, outputs, or weights by default (zero data retention for synchronous inference; async inputs stored only until processed, outputs never stored — docs.baseten.co/observability/security), which limits what customer personal data could be in backups at all.

3.1.4.notes: No Baseten page retrieved this session documents who generates or manages encryption keys, and no CMEK/BYOK offering was found. Asserting the playbook's managed-cloud default 'Key generated by Subprocessor (not customer-specific)' would be inference, not evidence — ask the vendor. Complication to resolve with the human: Baseten offers Self-hosted and Hybrid deployment models where workloads (and presumably keys) live in the customer's own cloud (baseten.co/deployments/baseten-self-hosted/, /baseten-hybrid/); the answer depends on which deployment model Tavus actually uses. Confirm Tavus's deployment model, then ask Baseten for the key-management scheme applicable to it.

3.1.6.notes: No primary source retrieved this session states that Baseten can anonymize customer personal data on the customer's instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) support). Domain-restricted searches for anonymize/pseudonymize/de-identify on baseten.co and docs.baseten.co surfaced nothing vendor-specific. Adjacent-but-different fact (do not conflate): Baseten's default zero-data-retention posture (inputs/outputs not stored by default) is deletion/minimization, not an anonymization capability.

3.1.7.notes: No mention of pseudonymization anywhere in retrieved Baseten material. Same search scope as 3.1.6.

3.1.8.value:
Zero data retention by default: model inputs and outputs are not stored by default (synchronous inference); for async inference, inputs are stored only temporarily until processed and outputs are never stored
Per-customer dedicated Kubernetes namespace with workload isolation enforced through Calico and Cilium; nodes run in private subnets with firewall protections
Annual penetration testing by independent third-party security firms; malicious model deployments tested in a dedicated prod-like environment
Encrypted secrets storage scoped to the customer workspace; secrets encrypted and injected into the model environment only at runtime
SSO via SAML 2.0 with major identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace, Azure AD) plus SCIM 2.0 directory sync; role-based access control on workspaces; scoped workspace/personal API keys with central admin revocation
Single-tenant, self-hosted, and hybrid deployment options that keep workloads and data in the customer's own cloud
Regional environments that route inference traffic exclusively to workload planes within a designated geographic region (US, EU, UK, Australia), guaranteeing data stays in the designated region
SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA compliant (both Baseten-hosted and self-hosted deployments)
3.1.8.locator: Assembled one-per-line from: docs.baseten.co/observability/security (zero data retention, Kubernetes namespace isolation via Calico/Cilium, private subnets/firewalls, annual third-party penetration testing, SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA), docs.baseten.co/organization/secrets (encrypted secrets), baseten.co/resources/changelog/sso-and-scim/ and docs.baseten.co/observability/access (SSO/SAML 2.0, SCIM, RBAC, API key management), baseten.co/deployments/baseten-self-hosted/ and /baseten-hybrid/ (single-tenant/self-hosted/hybrid), docs.baseten.co/deployment/regional-environments (region-locked routing)
3.1.8.notes: Every line traces to a baseten.co or docs.baseten.co page surfaced in domain-restricted search snippets this session; none of the pages could be fetched directly (gateway EGRESS_BLOCKED). Deliberately excludes anything only claimed by third parties or inferable from the underlying cloud providers Baseten runs on.

open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the exact legal entity that contracts for the Baseten service (full name, legal form, and state of incorporation — is it Baseten Labs, Inc., a Delaware corporation?) and the current registered address (your Terms state 201 Spear Street, Suite 1600, San Francisco, CA 94105).
Has Baseten designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address.

Does Baseten have a formally appointed Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide name, telephone number and/or email; if not, please confirm privacy@baseten.co as the contact entitled to respond to data-protection requests, and provide a telephone number if available.

What minimum TLS version is enforced for data in transit on Baseten inference and management endpoints (TLS 1.2 or 1.3), and is TLS also enforced for internal traffic between platform services and model pods?

Is customer data at rest (async inference inputs while queued, logs, secrets, custom model weights and source code) encrypted, with which algorithm (e.g. AES-256), and on which underlying cloud provider(s)?
Are backups of customer data taken, and if so are they encrypted and with which algorithm?

Who generates and manages the encryption keys for data at rest — Baseten/its cloud provider (shared or customer-specific keys), or can customers supply their own keys (CMEK/BYOK)? Please answer for the Baseten Cloud deployment model specifically.
Can Baseten anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer personal data on the customer's documented instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) GDPR support)?
Beyond SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA, does Baseten hold any of: ISO/IEC 27001, 27018, 27701, 9001, ISO 22301/BS 25999, SOC 1, SOC 3? Please provide current certificates/reports.

For the EU regional environment: does it cover the video/audio inference workloads Tavus runs on Baseten, does it guarantee both processing and storage stay in the EU/EEA, and what is required to enable it for our account?
